[Music] How to catch a turkey by Adam Wallace and Andy Elkton. Read by teacher Mike. Thanksgiving is here. It's time for feasts and family. But for one school, it's a time for a wild adventure. Gather around as I tell you a tale of a turkey on the loose. Here we are on Thanksgiving Day. It's that special time of the year. Yes, I know. I am a turkey. And that much should be clear. On Thanksgiving Day, our friend the turkey is not just any turkey. He's a superstar. He has photos of himself with important people and many shiny trophies and ribbons all around him. each telling a story of his victories, which simply means big wins. Look, there's a framed American football uniform called a jersey and it has a big T on it. What could the T stand for? Hm. Is it tea for turkey? Or could it be for Thanksgiving since it's a special time when turkeys are celebrated in America. So, gather around. I have a tale and it's really quite a story. What I tell you now is not a joke. It's my crowning glory. Why is the turkey showing us all these pictures and trophies? Do you think the turkey is proud of its achievements? Yay! It all began one year ago. I was at school, you see. Play preparations were underway, but that didn't matter to me. Everyone was buzzing with excitement. The children were getting ready to put on a play. They were dressed up in traditional clothing from a long, long time ago. Who were they pretending to be? The boy was wearing a tall hat and the girl was wearing a white wrap around her hair. They were both wearing dark clothing with a wide collar. The collar is the white fabric around their neck. The girl is wearing a nice white apron. Who wore these clothes a long time ago? Are there any more clues we can find? Behind them were lots of fruits and vegetables seemingly exploding out of a hornshaped basket. And behind those fruits and vegetables was a big rock. It said Plymouth Rock. Oh, this is the story about the pilgrims who sailed over on a big ship from England from a place called Plymouth when they arrived in America. They called their new home Plymouth as well. And it's also about the Native Americans who already lived in America. It's about the big feast that they had together and ate a big turkey. Oh no. Do you think the turkey knows why he's there? Some kids walked by in silly clothes talking about the play. We'll even have a turkey on stage. It's perfect for Thanksgiving Day. The turkey looked back and forth at all the children and the objects on stage. Our feathered friend was making the connection. Plymouth Rock, pilgrims, a harvest of fruits and vegetables, Thanksgiving Day. He realized he's on the menu. I'm not going to be part of the feast. The turkey paced back and forth and flapped his wings nervously as he thought, "Turkey stage. No way, no how. Had I really heard that right?" I broke out of my pen and ran away with a case of bad stage fright. I'm supposed to be part of the feast. Turkey wanted to be part of the celebration, but not part of the meal. What would you do if you were the turkey? I'm out of here. You're not eating me. He decided to escape. The turkey flapped his wings and went vroom. He ran so fast that everyone shouted, "LOOK, THE TURKEY is a loose." Where do you think the turkey might hide in the school? The turkey zoomed past into the science lab and oh boy did he make a mess. I burst into the science room and knocked over flasks and beers and the cry of catch that turkey boomed over the loudspeakers. Catch that turkey. A boy with robotic arms cried, "I can attract him with the magnets." [Music] But turkeys aren't made of metal, so the turkey won't be magnetic.
